newsitem.title: USA: Inland says price hikes difficult to get.
newsitem.headline: Inland says price hikes difficult to get.

text.p: Despite strong steel demand, price increases have been difficult to obtain due to highly competitive market conditions, the chairman of Inland Steel Industries Inc said Monday.

"The markets remain strong but price increases (on flat-rolled steel) have been difficult to get," Robert Darnall told reporters in a conference call following the release of Inland's second-quarter results.

Referring to the currently high level of imports entering the U.S. market, Darnall said conditions are "highly competitive." He said that has been pressuring prices, and as a result, a second-quarter price hike that Inland and other U.S. producers tried to push through on flat-rolled products did not hold in the market.
"The increase in the second quarter has not stuck," he said.

"Right now we see spot prices as stable," he added. "We're keeping our fingers crossed that prices stay stable in the third quarter. The picture right now is price stability, neither with an upward bias nor a downward bias."
Inland posted second-quarter earnings of $0.59 per share, excluding special items. Wall Street's consensus estimate was $0.64, with a range of $0.60 to $0.68, according to First Call.
In the year-earlier period, earnings were $0.25 per share, also excluding one-time items.
